raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Add complete Kimi K3 EPLB metadata and redundant-expert support for both the main Kimi Linear model and its MTP model.

This change makes Kimi K3 expose the model-level MoE metadata expected by the v1 EPLB controller, constructs FusedMoE/MegaMoE with the physical expert layout, loads checkpoint weights into redundant physical expert slots, and keeps physical-expert metadata synchronized after a rearrangement.

The implementation is intentionally model-specific. It does not change the generic EPLB policy, communication implementation, or scheduling algorithm.

## Why this change is needed

Before this PR, Kimi K3 instantiated its MoE layers without exposing the complete `MixtureOfExperts` contract used by EPLB:

- the model did not report its MoE layer list to `EplbState`;
- logical, physical, redundant, and rank-local expert counts were not tracked consistently;
- FusedMoE was not constructed with Kimi's EPLB/redundant-expert configuration;
- MegaMoE only allocated the original logical experts;
- checkpoint expert mappings did not populate redundant physical slots;
- the MTP MoE container did not register its expert layers with EPLB.

As a result, the generic EPLB controller could not safely build and update Kimi K3 expert maps.

## Implementation

### Main Kimi K3 model

`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py` now:

1. Derives the expert layout from the runtime parallel configuration:

   - `n_logical_experts` remains the checkpoint/model expert count;
   - `n_redundant_experts` comes from `EPLBConfig` when EPLB is enabled;
   - `n_physical_experts = n_logical_experts + n_redundant_experts`;
   - `n_local_physical_experts = n_physical_experts / ep_size`.

2. Validates physical-expert divisibility only for paths that require it: MegaMoE or EPLB. This avoids changing ordinary non-EPLB FusedMoE behavior.

3. Constructs MegaMoE with the physical expert count and correct rank-local physical range.

4. Constructs FusedMoE with:

   ```python
   enable_eplb=self.enable_eplb
   num_redundant_experts=self.n_redundant_experts
   ```

5. Includes redundant physical slots in `fused_moe_make_expert_params_mapping`, so every redundant replica receives its initial logical-expert checkpoint weights.

6. Adds `KimiK3MixtureOfExperts`, which exposes the model-level metadata required by EPLB:

   - `moe_mlp_layers`;
   - `moe_layers`;
   - `num_moe_layers`;
   - logical/physical/local/redundant expert counts;
   - routed/shared expert counts;
   - expert-group count.

7. Implements `update_physical_experts_metadata()` so the model and individual Kimi MoE layers remain synchronized when the physical layout changes.

8. Makes `KimiLinearForCausalLM` implement this shared Kimi K3 MoE interface and registers every real, non-PP-placeholder Kimi MoE layer.

### MTP model

`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mtp.py` now:

- makes `KimiK3MTP` implement `KimiK3MixtureOfExperts`;
- registers all MTP MoE layers with the same metadata path as the main model;
- includes redundant expert slots when constructing the MTP checkpoint expert mapping.

This keeps main-model and MTP expert registration consistent without duplicating EPLB bookkeeping logic.

## Expert layout example used in validation

The full Kimi K3 checkpoint contains 896 logical routed experts.

With EPLB enabled in the validation run:

```text
logical experts:    896
redundant experts:   16
physical experts:   912
EP size:              16
physical slots/rank:  57
```

The control run retained the original identity layout:

```text
logical experts:    896
redundant experts:    0
physical experts:   896
EP size:              16
physical slots/rank:  56
```

## End-to-end validation configuration

Two full GSM8K runs were executed. They used the same model, image, hardware topology, parallelism, model limits, weight-loading configuration, and request workload. The functional difference was whether EPLB rearrangement was enabled.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` |
| Model revision | `79a424f302e6ed63cd82211b0e99918cdb6de8df` |
| Runtime image | `kimi-k3-oss-0723-arm64-cu130-ubuntu2404-commit-e3e837.sqsh` |
| Service nodes | 4 × GB200 nodes, 4 GPUs/node |
| Client node | 1 additional node |
| Tensor parallelism | TP4 |
| Data parallelism | DP4 |
| Expert parallelism | EP16 |
| GPU memory utilization | 0.85 |
| MTP | disabled for this main-model comparison |
| GSM8K test questions | 1319 |
| Few-shot examples | 5 |
| Client concurrency | 128 |
| Maximum output tokens | 1024 |
| Maximum model length | 2944 |
| Maximum sequences | 256 |
| Weight loader | `fastsafetensors` |
| Safetensors strategy | `lazy` |
| `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE` | 1 |
| EPLB load window | 32 steps |
| EPLB rearrangement interval | 64 steps |
| EPLB policy | `default` |
| EPLB communicator | `torch_gloo` |
| EPLB mode | synchronous (`use_async=false`) |

Exact EPLB-enabled configuration:

```json
{
  "window_size": 32,
  "step_interval": 64,
  "num_redundant_experts": 16,
  "log_balancedness": true,
  "log_balancedness_interval": 16,
  "use_async": false,
  "policy": "default",
  "communicator": "torch_gloo"
}
```

Exact observation-only control configuration:

```json
{
  "window_size": 32,
  "step_interval": 64,
  "num_redundant_experts": 0,
  "log_balancedness": true,
  "log_balancedness_interval": 16,
  "use_async": false,
  "policy": "default",
  "communicator": "torch_gloo"
}
```

The control retained the load-accounting instrumentation and identity expert map but performed no expert rearrangement, weight movement, or map commit.

## Full GSM8K results

| Metric | EPLB enabled (job 10272) | Observation-only control (job 10300) | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Correct answers | 1260 / 1319 | 1256 / 1319 | Four-answer difference |
| Accuracy | 95.5269% | 95.2237% | 0.3032 percentage-point difference |
| Request errors | 0 | 0 | Both runs completed cleanly |
| Evaluation latency | 1466.50 s | 463.11 s | Synchronous rearrangement dominates EPLB wall time |
| Questions/s | 0.8994 | 2.8481 | Control is 3.17× faster |
| Output tokens/s | 91.37 | 291.66 | Control is 3.19× faster |
| Rank-load samples | 97 | 97 | Same observation cadence |
| Median rank balancedness | 0.9919 | 0.9356 | EPLB substantially improves rank balance |
| High-load median balancedness | 0.9947 | 0.9374 | Same conclusion under sustained load |
| Median max/mean rank load | 1.008× | 1.069× | EPLB reduces the hottest-rank excess |
| Completed formal rearrangements | 24 | 0 | Profile rearrangement excluded |
| Rank-level map commits | 384 | 0 | 24 rearrangements × 16 EP ranks |

### Rank-load metric

The figure and reported balancedness use the raw 16-rank arrays emitted by the experiment:

```text
[EPLB_TRACE] rank_load ... rank_tokens=[rank0, ..., rank15]
```

Rank balancedness is calculated as:

```text
mean(rank_tokens) / max(rank_tokens)
```

This is deliberately calculated from `rank_tokens` rather than reusing the generic `EPLB step: balancedness=...` log field, because this experiment specifically measures aggregate EP-rank imbalance.

### Rearrangement cost

The EPLB run produced 24 formal `committed=True` rearrangements during the evaluation:

- cumulative CUDA-event-measured rearrangement time: **933.8124 seconds**;
- median rearrangement duration: **38.88 seconds**;
- maximum rearrangement duration: **39.87 seconds**;
- total EPLB evaluation wall time: **1466.50 seconds**;
- control evaluation wall time: **463.11 seconds**;
- wall-time difference: **1003.39 seconds**.

The measured rearrangement GPU time is 63.7% of the EPLB run's complete wall time and is close to the observed wall-time difference. The CUDA-event value is not claimed to be a complete wall-clock measurement: CPU coordination, collectives, and scheduling can add additional time.

Because this run used `use_async=false`, every rearrangement was on the synchronous inference path:

```text
EplbState.step()
  -> EplbState.rearrange()
  -> rearrange_expert_weights_inplace()
  -> commit expert maps
  -> resume forward execution
```

The generic EPLB implementation also has an asynchronous worker mode, but async EPLB was not evaluated in these two runs and no async performance claim is made here.

## Timeline and comparison image

![Kimi K3 EPLB GSM8K comparison](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/blob/806149b88868cda5afac8405437f1124caa3d1a2/docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-comparison.png?raw=true)

The red bands are the 24 formal synchronous rearrangement periods. Each band is labelled with the CUDA-event duration from its corresponding `committed=True` log entry. The lower panel shows the cumulative measured GPU rearrangement time.

The figure intentionally omits separate throughput and latency bar charts; all exact end-to-end values are listed in the results table above.

## Uploaded experiment record

A detailed, repository-backed experiment record is included here:

- [`docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-experiment.md`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/blob/806149b88868cda5afac8405437f1124caa3d1a2/docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-experiment.md)
- [`docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-comparison.png`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/blob/806149b88868cda5afac8405437f1124caa3d1a2/docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-comparison.png)

Local raw artifacts retained for reproducibility:

- EPLB server log: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/results/k3-full-gsm8k-eplb-load-10272/serve-srun.log`
- Control server log: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/results/k3-full-gsm8k-eplb-load-10300/serve-srun.log`
- EPLB GSM8K summary: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/results/k3-full-gsm8k-eplb-load-10272/gsm8k-full.json`
- Control GSM8K summary: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/results/k3-full-gsm8k-eplb-load-10300/gsm8k-full.json`
- EPLB load analysis: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/results/k3-full-gsm8k-eplb-load-10272/load-imbalance.json`
- Control load analysis: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/results/k3-full-gsm8k-eplb-load-10300/load-imbalance.json`
- Plot generator: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/scripts/plot_eplb_comparison.py`
- Experiment launcher: `/home/inf-aoshen/vllm/projects/vllm-rl-day0-support/k3/agent_run/scripts/run_k3_full_gsm8k_eplb_load_imbalance.sbatch`

## Limitations and follow-up work

- The current `rank_load` window aggregates prefill and decode tokens. It does not yet produce separate prefill-only and decode-only imbalance statistics.
- This comparison validates synchronous EPLB only. Async EPLB requires a separate experiment.
- The observation-only load accounting used for the control run was an experiment overlay and is not part of this model-support PR.
- The runtime experiments used the PR commit as their model-support baseline plus temporary observability instrumentation. The PR itself remains limited to the Kimi K3 model/MTP support and the uploaded experiment documentation.
- The comparison demonstrates that the rearrangement algorithm improves rank balance, but the tested `step_interval=64` synchronous configuration is too expensive for this workload. This is a configuration/runtime-policy result, not a correctness failure in the Kimi K3 registration patch.

## Validation

Implementation checks completed before the original PR commit:

```bash
python -m py_compile vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py
python -m py_compile vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mtp.py
pre-commit run
```

Documentation/image commit checks:

```bash
git diff --check
pre-commit run --files \
  docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-experiment.md \
  docs/eplb/kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-comparison.png
```

The staged-file pre-commit run passed, including markdownlint, typo checking, PNG validation, and repository configuration checks.

Runtime verification:

- both 1319-question GSM8K evaluations completed with zero request errors;
- job 10272 passed the EPLB event verifier;
- job 10300 passed the observation-only verifier;
- the EPLB run recorded model registration, prepare-forward, rearrangement trigger, load aggregation, new mapping, map commit, and completion events;
- the control run recorded 97 rank-load samples and zero rearrangement/map-commit events.

## Duplicate-work check

No open `vllm-project/vllm` PR matching `Kimi K3 EPLB` was found at the time this description was updated. Within `Inferact/mke`, this PR is the existing Kimi K3 EPLB integration rather than a duplicate implementation.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for code review support, experiment orchestration, log analysis, visualization generation, and drafting this description. The submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line, validating the experiment interpretation, and defending the implementation and results.

+# Kimi K3 EPLB experiment
+
+This document records the reproducible configuration and the two full GSM8K
+runs used to validate the Kimi K3 EPLB integration in this pull request.
+
+## Code scope
+
+The PR changes only the Kimi K3 model and MTP model metadata paths:
+
+- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py`
+    - derives logical, physical, local, and redundant expert counts from the
+    parallel and EPLB configuration;
+    - passes physical expert counts and the initial physical-to-logical layout
+    to MegaMoE and FusedMoE;
+    - includes redundant physical slots in checkpoint expert-parameter mapping;
+    - exposes `KimiK3MixtureOfExperts` metadata and physical-expert update
+    methods to the v1 EPLB controller.
+- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mtp.py`
+    - registers MTP MoE layers with the same EPLB metadata interface;
+    - includes redundant physical slots when building MTP expert mappings.
+
+The implementation keeps the logical expert count unchanged. With
+`num_redundant_experts=16`, 896 logical experts become 912 physical slots,
+distributed as 57 physical slots per EP rank at EP16. With EPLB disabled, the
+layout is the original 896 experts / 56 slots per rank.
+
+## Runtime configuration
+
+Both runs used the same model, image, parallelism, request workload, and
+loading path. The only functional difference was whether EPLB rearrangement
+was enabled.
+
+| Setting | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Model | `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` |
+| Model revision | `79a424f302e6ed63cd82211b0e99918cdb6de8df` |
+| Image | `kimi-k3-oss-0723-arm64-cu130-ubuntu2404-commit-e3e837.sqsh` |
+| Service nodes | 4 |
+| Client/publisher node | 1 |
+| Tensor parallelism | TP4 |
+| Data parallelism | DP4 |
+| Expert parallelism | EP16 |
+| GPU memory utilization | 0.85 |
+| MTP | disabled |
+| GSM8K questions | 1319 |
+| Few-shot examples | 5 |
+| Client concurrency | 128 |
+| Maximum output tokens | 1024 |
+| Maximum model length | 2944 |
+| Maximum sequences | 256 |
+| Weight format | `fastsafetensors` |
+| Safetensors strategy | `lazy` |
+| Fast safetensors queue | 1 |
+| EPLB window | 32 |
+| EPLB step interval | 64 |
+| EPLB policy | `default` |
+| EPLB communicator | `torch_gloo` |
+| EPLB async mode | `false` |
+
+### EPLB-enabled run (job 10272)
+
+```text
+logical experts:   896
+redundant experts:  16
+physical experts:  912
+enable_eplb:       1
+observe_only:      0
+```
+
+### Observation-only control run (job 10300)
+
+This run retained the load-accounting and `rank_load` instrumentation but used
+the identity expert map and performed no rearrangement or weight movement.
+
+```text
+logical experts:   896
+redundant experts:  0
+physical experts:  896
+enable_eplb:       0
+observe_only:      1
+```
+
+## Results
+
+| Metric | EPLB enabled (10272) | Observation-only (10300) |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| GSM8K correct | 1260 / 1319 | 1256 / 1319 |
+| Accuracy | 95.5269% | 95.2237% |
+| Evaluation latency | 1466.50 s | 463.11 s |
+| Questions per second | 0.8994 | 2.8481 |
+| Output tokens per second | 91.37 | 291.66 |
+| Rank-load samples | 97 | 97 |
+| Median rank balancedness | 0.9919 | 0.9356 |
+| Median max/mean rank load | 1.008x | 1.069x |
+| Formal rearrangements | 24 | 0 |
+| Map commits | 384 | 0 |
+
+Rank balancedness is calculated from the raw 16-rank `rank_tokens` arrays as:
+
+```text
+mean(rank_tokens) / max(rank_tokens)
+```
+
+The EPLB run performed 24 formal synchronous rearrangements. Their
+CUDA-event-measured durations sum to 933.8124 seconds; the median individual
+duration was 38.88 seconds and the maximum was 39.87 seconds. This explains
+the dominant runtime difference between the two runs: the total latency
+difference is 1003.39 seconds, while the measured rearrangement GPU time is
+933.81 seconds.
+
+The load data is aggregate window data. It does not currently separate
+prefill and decode because the existing EPLB load pass combines both phases
+before emitting `rank_load`.
+
+## Reproduction artifacts
+
+The comparison image is included in this PR:
+
+![Kimi K3 EPLB GSM8K comparison](kimi-k3-eplb-gsm8k-comparison.png)
+
+The image shows:
+
+1. rank balancedness over the evaluation timeline for both runs;
+2. every completed synchronous rearrangement as a red time band, with its
